title: Mathematical billiards
summary: Convex billiard tables of class C^k in ℂ, the billiard ball map on the phase cylinder (regularity, closed-cylinder extension, time reversal, comparison with SymplecticGeometry/CotangentLagrangian C3.1), its generating function and invariant measure, twist maps of the annulus, rotational invariant curves with Birkhoff's Lipschitz graph theorem (Fathi's topological proof) and rotation numbers, two Birkhoff periodic orbits of every type (p, q); polygonal tables with holes, the singular set, the almost-everywhere billiard flow as a measure-preserving ℝ-action, rational tables and non-ergodicity, translation surfaces with directional flows, the Katok–Zemlyakov surface (cone angles, genus, unfolding conjugacy), and weak mixing of flows with its eigenfunction criterion.

targets.name: Billiards.ConvexTable
targets.statement: A convex billiard table of class C^k (k : ℕ∞, k ≥ 1): ℓ > 0 and γ : ℝ → ℂ, C^k, ℓ-periodic, ‖γ′‖ = 1, injective on [0, ℓ), with τ(s) × (γ t − γ s) > 0 whenever t − s ∉ ℓℤ, where τ = γ′ and a × b = Im(conj a · b). Ω is the closed convex hull of the image.

api.name: isJordanCurve_range
api.statement: The image of γ is a Jordan curve; γ descends to a homeomorphism of AddCircle ℓ onto it; γ s = γ t iff t − s ∈ ℓℤ.

api.name: strictConvex_hull
api.statement: Ω is compact with nonempty interior, StrictConvex ℝ Ω, frontier Ω = range γ, and Ω minus γ(s) lies in the open half-plane left of the tangent at γ(s).

api.name: shift_rigid
api.statement: s ↦ γ(s + c) and z ↦ a z + b (|a| = 1) preserve tables; s ↦ γ(−s) never gives a table.

api.name: curvature_nonneg
api.statement: For k ≥ 2 the signed curvature κ = τ × τ′ is ≥ 0.

api.name: mono
api.statement: A table of class C^k is a table of class C^j for j ≤ k.

The differential condition is preserved when r is a C¹ diffeomorphism.

targets.name: Billiards.IsExactTwist
targets.statement: A monotone twist map is exact for λ=g dx (g C¹, ℓ-periodic, ∂y g=ρ>0) when F*λ−λ=dS with S ℓ-periodic C¹. Put Q(x,y)=(x,F₁(x,y)), a C¹ diffeomorphism from ℝ×J onto its open image D={(x,X): X∈F₁(x,J)}. Equivalently h=S∘Q⁻¹:D→ℝ, S=h∘Q, is diagonal-deck-invariant and satisfies g(x,y)=−∂₁h(x,F₁(x,y)), g(F(x,y))=∂₂h(x,F₁(x,y)). This endpoint-coordinate deduction is constructed here from the globally canonical setting.

locator.where: Chapitre I, §4.3, Remarque, printed p.27, lines 762–769 (globally canonical setting); endpoint-coordinate construction is here

targets.name: Billiards.ConvexTable.exists_max_periodic
targets.statement: W attains its maximum on D̄_{p,q} only at points of D_{p,q}; every maximiser is a periodic orbit of type (p, q). In the boundary proof, exclude W=0 using any positive-perimeter interior configuration. If W>0, an endpoint of a maximal run of geometrically coincident vertices adjoins a nondegenerate chord: for a preceding gap 0 increase that endpoint, for a preceding gap ℓ decrease it (reverse the signs for a following gap). The collapsed chord contributes +1, and the other chord has derivative of absolute value <1, giving 1±cos δ>0 within the gap constraints.

At a collapsed limit exactly p gaps equal ℓ and q−p equal 0; d_j(t)=(1−t)d_j+t pℓ/q has right perimeter derivative 2p(q−p)ℓ/q>0. These directions persist with positive derivative nearby; add a sufficiently small equal-gap inward direction in the run-end case and combine by a partition of unity.

targets.name: Billiards.isWeaklyMixing_iff
